definition: A decoding parameter that sharpens or flattens the token probability distribution, controlling randomness.
details: A low temperature makes the most probable tokens even more likely, producing repetitive, focused text; a high temperature flattens the distribution for more varied and creative output. Temperature is one of several sampling controls (with top-k and nucleus/top-p) studied for improving the quality of open-ended neural text generation.
story: Picture a novelist who has read so much that, given a first line, they cannot help but write the next one. Here is the short version: A decoding parameter that sharpens or flattens the token probability distribution, controlling randomness. The part that makes it sing: A low temperature makes the most probable tokens even more likely, producing repetitive, focused text; a high temperature flattens the distribution for more varied and creative output. It is prediction pushed forward — each next word, or pixel, guessed from everything that came before it. And that is Temperature — making something new out of everything it has ever seen.

citation.title: The Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration
